note: Evidence, never a quarantine list: no build, test run or CI step reads this file (scripts/test-diag-coverage.py enforces that), so an entry cannot skip, retry or excuse a test. A first failure is recorded with its signature and reruns; a clean rerun does not establish a root cause, and an entry stays nonreproduced until its explanation is shown.

failures.lane: win-asan (local, inside vcvars; hosted twice: nightly run 39013990584 at d08436b9, 2026-10-17, and push run 39129062998 at 9461800a, 2026-10-18)
failures.signature: AddressSanitizer use-after-poison (shadow f7, poisoned by user) in a memset inside RtlCreateHeap, reached from msvcrt.dll loaded during exit() after main returned (exe_common.inl line 295), 0.11-0.25 s after launch
failures.reruns: Local: the immediate rerun passed; the next run of the same seed was clean. Hosted: the next nightly run at the same revision (39108972918) passed the job; it failed again in 39129062998. It depends on the OS mapping the new heap where the arena had been.
failures.explanation: A Cerid defect. VirtualMemoryAllocator poisons its committed tail and released its reservation without unpoisoning, assuming the runtime clears an unmapped range's shadow; the Windows runtime keeps it (the Linux one clears it on munmap), so when exit() loaded msvcrt.dll and its heap was mapped at addresses an arena of the corpus had released, the interceptor's memset hit the stale poison. purge() also left its decommitted tail poisoned. Both now unpoison (purge what it decommits, the destructor [0, commit_pos)); a crd-memory-tests case and the corpus replay itself check the released range's shadow, and each fails with either half removed on win-asan (the purge half on linux-gcc-asan too); 2026-10-18-diag-11b-build-speed-compile-time.md.

failures.target: crd-fuzz-perf-flight, crd-fuzz-perf-bundle, crd-fuzz-ceir-differential, crd-fuzz-ceir-text, crd-fuzz-ckir-binary and the plain corpus replays
failures.signature: Wild jumps with corrupted registers and locals; ASan SEGV writing address 4 in asan_annotate_live_range; a container overflow on a byte push_back had just marked usable; MallocAllocator's power-of-two check failing on the constant 8; once a silently wrong result in an unsanitized gcc build

failures.explanation: Input-independent and seen with the container annotation off, outside libFuzzer and without a sanitizer, so the evidence points at this machine (CPU or WSL guest), not Cerid code. Not settled: the separating run on another machine is the user's item in DIAG.10a.

failures.target: lld-link of large test executables (thin LTO)
failures.signature: lld-link 20.1.8 crashes with 0xC0000005 or Illegal instruction while running LTO codegen of a module unrelated to the change; no source diagnostic

failures.signature: Six node bounds (max.x, max.y, max.z) differed between the CPU and GPU builds by 0.003 to 0.049 against a 1-ULP tolerance (test_lbvh.cpp:487-489); 169,984 of 169,990 assertions passed
failures.reruns: Run alone it then passed once and 10 of 10 with --repeat until-fail:10.

failures.target: crd-jobs-tests: tsan harness: the data-race specimen is caught, or reported absent
failures.signature: Verdict Timeout (exceeded 10000 ms) instead of SanitizerCaught; the specimen sat in a futex wait with near-zero CPU, its racing thread blocked in __tsan::ReportRace reading from the llvm-symbolizer child
failures.reruns: Reproduced on an immediate rerun of the same exe and when run directly; with DEBUGINFOD_URLS unset it was caught in 0.05 s and the whole program passed (188 cases).
failures.explanation: The login shell sets DEBUGINFOD_URLS (Ubuntu's profile.d), so llvm-symbolizer-18 waited on an unreachable debuginfod server after a WSL restart. The specimen links only Threads; no Cerid code is involved. Local WSL scripts now unset the variable; hosted steps are non-login shells.

failures.lane: every hosted Linux lane (linux-gcc-debug, -public-checks, -debug-scalar, -debug-sse2, -asan, -release, -relwithdebinfo, linux-clang-tsan), run 38209499793
failures.target: diag10c: the resident reading follows memory this process touches (crd-core-tests)
failures.signature: CHECK( after.resident.high_water >= peak ) failed: 72708096 >= 72777728, 17 pages short, after 64 MiB was touched and released
failures.reruns: Not seen on this host's WSL2 guest (kernel 6.6, 32 CPUs): 200 runs of the case before the fix; 100 runs of the host-pressure cases after it.
failures.explanation: Probable mechanism, not observed here: the kernel sums VmRSS approximately from per-CPU counters and records VmHWM from such a sum only at some points, so a later VmHWM can be below an earlier VmRSS, and the reading reported max(VmHWM, VmRSS) for each call. read_host_memory now reports a process-wide peak (an atomic maximum) that cannot fall between readings, whatever the kernel's counters do.

failures.target: CEIR-17d GATE: the shipped GPU-cull config's device verdict EQUALS the CPU cull (Vulkan) (crd-scene-render-tests)
failures.signature: ThreadSanitizer data race: operator delete on llvmpipe-3 against operator new (llvm::allocate_buffer) on llvmpipe-0, both access stacks only the allocator interceptors and libLLVM.so.20.1; the threads were created by libvulkan_lvp.so under vkCreateDevice
failures.reruns: Not seen on this host's WSL2 guest: through ctest on linux-clang-tsan the gate passed 60 of 60 runs with the previous suppression file and 60 of 60 with the new one.
failures.explanation: Inside Mesa lavapipe's LLVM JIT, which is not built with TSan, so its own hand-offs are invisible; no Cerid frame is in either access stack and nothing in Cerid links LLVM. race:libLLVM.so is now in tests/support/diag/tsan-suppressions.txt under the file's third-party rule.
